capture.final_message:
Choose a fixed \(A\in(0,\tfrac12]\). For the first conjunct, use the Euler–Maclaurin/truncated Dirichlet-series representation of \(\zeta(s)\), truncating at \(N\asymp |t|\). When
\[
1-\frac{A}{\log |t|}\le \sigma\le 2,
\]
one has \(N^{1-\sigma}\le e^A\), so the truncated sum and remainder are uniformly \(O(\log |t|)\). Enlarging the constant handles the bounded range \(|t|>3\), yielding a single \(C>0\).

For \(\psi(x)\sim x\), use
\[
-\frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^s}.
\]
The Hadamard–de la Vallée Poussin argument shows that \(\zeta\) has no zeros on \(\Re s=1\). Thus \(-\zeta'/\zeta\) has only the simple pole at \(s=1\), with residue \(1\), along that boundary. Applying Wiener–Ikehara to the nonnegative coefficients \(\Lambda(n)\) gives
\(\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)=\psi(x)\sim x\). The condition \(|t|>3\) ensures \(\log|t|>0\) throughout the first estimate.
